statements.markdown: Landau’s classical theorem [Lan05] concerns a Dirichlet series with non-negative coeffi- cients and needs the bound for all large x. The windowed form is what lets the rest of the proof work only at scales where suitable auxiliary fields exist. Its proof takes the Laplace transform of v 7→ G(e v ) and looks at its Taylor coefficients at a real point s 0 ; the coefficient of order N is an integral of G against a Gamma kernel which, for N ≈ (1 + ω/2)s 0 log Y , is concentrated in the window. A zero to the right of θ contributes a residue of a definite sign and makes these coefficients grow; a two-case argument on whether the zero nearest to s 0 is real handles complex zeros. The only input from the theory of L-functions is non-vanishing on Re s ≥ 1.

lean.name: Deduction.landau_window
lean.note: The proof bounds Laplace coefficients with a concentrated kernel. It uses a positive residue at an isolated real pole or the residue norm at a shifted complex center.

lean.name: Deduction.lemmaL
lean.plain: Apply the window bound to a character family
lean.note: This step supplies pole data for the character family, applies the window argument to its zeros, and invokes known nonvanishing for real part at least one.
